All-New Buick LaCrosse Sedan Breaks Cover in China and This Is What America Is Missing
10 photos
Photo: Buick
The 2027 Buick LaCrosse has officially launched in China. While the exterior design retains the familiar lines, the executive sedan hides completely new electrical architecture, a radically overhauled cabin layout, and sits on a highly advanced platform. The Buick LaCrosse remains exclusively manufactured in China for the Chinese market.
The exterior design has evolved with only minor changes from the fourth generation. The model now gets a broader, low-mounted front grille, updated bumper styling, sleek hidden exhaust tips, and sharper front and rear lamps that make it look wider, without altering its classic silhouette.
In the meantime, the proportions have remained unchanged, which means that the all-new Buick LaCrosse still measures 196.9 inches (5,003 millimeters) in length and sits on a wheelbase of 114.3 inches (2,905 millimeters)
However, the architecture underneath is completely new. The 2027 Buick LaCrosse has migrated onto SAIC-GM's next-generation platform, which made its debut back in 2025 with the Electra sub-brand's electrified vehicle lineup.
Photo: Buick However, the platform has been heavily adapted to house internal combustion engines while supporting advanced digital technology. The cabin is where the new generation marks its biggest shift. Buick has stripped out the previous layout to make room for over 50 premium upgrades, focused on luxury, comfort, and technology.
The 2027 LaCrosse gets a whole new massive floating center infotainment screen, alongside a digital instrument cluster, running on Qualcomm Snapdragon 8155 architecture for lightning-fast voice control responses of under 0.3 seconds and cloud connectivity. The new setup replaces the older curved screen layout.
The steering wheel, center console, and seating have been entirely redesigned. Now the premium seats feature multi-density 3D foam with extended thigh support. Upper trims pack active multi-stage ventilation and heating, along with six-point pneumatic massage functions in all four seats.
The powertrain is carried over unchanged. The 2027 Buick LaCrosse is powered by the eighth-generation Ecotec 2.0-liter turbocharged inline-four, which produces 233 horsepower (237 metric horsepower) and 258 pound-feet (350 Newton meters) of torque for a run from 0 to 60 mph in 7.2 seconds and a top speed of 143 mph (230 kph). A nine-speed automatic transmission puts the power down through the front wheels.
Photo: Buick A Level 2+ e-Cruise suite drives 14 active assistance systems, with capabilities for lane centering, full-speed adaptive cruise control, traffic jam assist, forward collision warning, and automated parking.
Buick sells the LaCrosse in two distinct trims. The LaCrosse Smart Edition starts at 149,900 yuan, which translates to roughly $22,500, and the Supreme Edition, which is a 169,900-yuan ($25,500) deal.
The all-new 2027 LaCrosse has already started rolling out to Buick's dealership network across China. There are currently no plans to reintroduce the LaCrosse to North America, where Buick has transitioned to an all- SUV brand lineup. The sedan was retired from the U.S. market after the 2019 model year.
